body.why: Without a cost gate in judge.py, P5's 24/7 loop optimizes accuracy by burning 30-60x more compute than baselines.
113 dev-only iterations need a pre-registered held-out test checkpoint in ledger/ to rule out dev overfitting.
Untrusted valgrind runs in confine mode lack rlimits and /w disk has no total quota.
An allowlist for infer.c eliminates residual Linux syscall surface left by a denylist.
Projected-only neuron checks allow single-run overshoots against free-tier daily limits.
Hardcoded pilot branch and dated audit path create unnecessary coupling for future queues.
Exact-line canary grading tests narrow phrasing rather than general worker robustness.
Unexplained 0.980 vs 0.977 mlp16 dev accuracy creates apparent baseline drift for readers.
P5 accuracy-vs-cost alignment (F001, F007) is the highest-leverage fix for Exagium's core thesis.
